data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: address
sections.question: address
sections.summary: the details of where someone lives or works

senses.definition: the details of the house or flat, street, and town where someone lives or works
examples: She wrote her name and address on the form to receive the newsletter.
Can you give me your address so I can send you the invitation?

senses.definition: to speak or write to someone directly
examples: She addressed the letter to her grandmother.
He addressed the audience at the beginning of the meeting.

answers.answer: She wrote her name and address on the form to receive the newsletter.
He cooked his address for dinner and served it with rice.
She drove her address to the office and left it at the desk.
They planted an address in the garden and watered it each morning.

sections.title: age
sections.question: age
sections.summary: how many years someone has lived; how old someone is

senses.definition: the number of years that someone has lived or that something has existed
examples: The form asked for her name, date of birth, and age.
At the age of eighteen, she moved to a new city to study.

answers.answer: The form asked for her name, date of birth, and age.
He cooked his age in a large pot for Sunday dinner.
She drove her age to the supermarket every Saturday.
They planted their age in the garden and watered it daily.

sections.title: birthday
sections.question: birthday
sections.summary: the anniversary of the day when someone was born

senses.definition: the anniversary of the day when someone was born, often celebrated with a party or gifts
examples: She celebrated her birthday with her family at a restaurant.
He sent her a card and flowers on her birthday.

answers.answer: She celebrated her birthday with her family at a restaurant.
He cooked a birthday for dinner every Tuesday evening.
She drove her birthday to work and parked it outside.
They planted a birthday in the garden and watered it daily.

sections.title: brush teeth
sections.question: brush teeth
sections.summary: to clean your teeth by moving a toothbrush backwards and forwards over them

partsOfSpeech.inflectionsLine: brushes teeth, brushing teeth, brushed teeth

senses.definition: to clean your teeth by moving a toothbrush over them, usually with toothpaste
examples: She brushes her teeth twice a day to keep them clean and healthy.
He always brushes his teeth after breakfast before going to school.

answers.answer: She brushes her teeth twice a day to keep them clean and healthy.
He brushes his teeth with a fork and a spoon after dinner.
She brushes her teeth to go shopping at the mall.
They brush their teeth in order to cook dinner in the kitchen.

sections.title: email
sections.question: email
sections.summary: a message sent electronically from one person to another via the internet

senses.definition: a message sent electronically from one person to another via the internet; also, the system used to send these messages
examples: She gave her email address so they could send her the confirmation.
He checks his email every morning when he arrives at the office.

senses.definition: to send a message to someone using the internet
examples: She emailed her manager to say she would be late.
Please email me the details when you have a moment.

answers.answer: She gave her email address so they could send her the confirmation.
He cooked an email for dinner and served it with salad.
She wore her email to the party and everyone admired it.
They planted an email in the garden near the flowers.

sections.title: gender
sections.question: gender
sections.summary: whether a person is male or female

senses.definition: the fact of being male or female; the social and cultural characteristics associated with being male or female
examples: The form asked for her name, nationality, and gender.
The survey included questions about age, gender, and occupation.

answers.answer: The form asked for her name, nationality, and gender.
He cooked the gender for dinner and served it with rice.
She drove her gender to work every morning.
They planted the gender in the garden and watered it daily.

sections.title: go to work
sections.question: go to work
sections.summary: to travel to the place where you do your job

partsOfSpeech.inflectionsLine: goes to work, going to work, went to work

senses.definition: to travel from your home to the place where you do your job
examples: She goes to work by bicycle every morning because she lives nearby.
He goes to work at eight o'clock and comes home at six.

answers.answer: She goes to work by bicycle every morning because she lives nearby.
He goes to work at the swimming pool to play football.
She goes to work at the supermarket to cook dinner.
They go to work at the park to eat breakfast outside.

sections.title: have breakfast
sections.question: have breakfast
sections.summary: to eat your first meal of the day

partsOfSpeech.inflectionsLine: has breakfast, having breakfast, had breakfast

senses.definition: to eat the first meal of the day, usually in the morning
examples: She always has breakfast before leaving the house in the morning.
He had breakfast at a café near the office before his meeting.

answers.answer: She always has breakfast before leaving the house in the morning.
He has breakfast at the swimming pool while doing laps.
She has breakfast on her bicycle on the way to work.
They have breakfast in the garden in order to water the plants.

sections.title: language
sections.question: language
sections.summary: a system of words and grammar used by people of a particular country or group

senses.definition: a system of words and grammar used by the people of a particular country or group to communicate
examples: She is studying a new language to help her find a job abroad.
English is the most widely spoken language in the world.

answers.answer: She is studying a new language to help her find a job abroad.
He cooked a language for dinner on Sunday evening.
She drove her language to school every morning.
They planted a language in the garden near the gate.

sections.title: marital status
sections.question: marital status
sections.summary: whether someone is married, single, divorced, or widowed

senses.definition: whether a person is single, married, divorced, or widowed
examples: The form asked for her name, age, address, and marital status.
He wrote 'married' in the marital status box on the application form.

answers.answer: The form asked for her name, age, address, and marital status.
He cooked the marital status for dinner and served it hot.
She drove her marital status to the office every day.
They planted marital status in the garden and watered it daily.
